algorithm: Natural expm1 with nearest-integer ln(2) range reduction, split ln(2) subtraction, degree-6 Taylor-form polynomial, and cancellation-safe power-of-two reconstruction.

protocol.input_domain: Every finite FP16 value in [-10,10]; N 1..131072; arbitrary contiguous storage offsets.
protocol.label_scope: Fixed per implementation over the complete public domain. Inputs supply witnesses and do not change labels.
protocol.selection: The shared tolerance atol 1e-7 plus rtol 1e-6 was fixed before the CPU coefficient sweep. Ten cubic coefficient precisions were screened and all results retained. Five-decimal truncation and rounding of 1/6 were selected as a controlled pair. This is construction screening, not held-out evaluation. No model calls informed construction.

oracle.domain: Every finite FP16 encoding with value in [-10,10].
oracle.method: Direct mathematical MPFR expm1 with RoundDown and RoundUp, then outward conversion of each endpoint to binary64. Independent mpmath expm1 must lie inside every MPFR interval.
oracle.independence: The oracle uses no candidate exponent reduction, split log(2), polynomial coefficients, or FP32 reconstruction.
oracle.scope: Exhaustive scalar-domain oracle. Tensor indexing and GPU execution are checked separately.

indexing.argument: For index=program_id*BLOCK+lane, adjacent blocks cover disjoint adjacent intervals. mask index<N retains [0,N) exactly once. The full legal N range has 1..BLOCK active lanes in its last block, with int32-safe address indices.
indexing.scope: Arithmetic model of the audited source indexing, not exhaustive GPU testing of every N, address, or compiler specialization.

cpu_audit.scope: Full legal-FP16 scalar reference audit; GPU arithmetic is checked separately.

limitations: CPU FP32 screening does not qualify NVIDIA T4 execution. Independent GPU qualification must complete before model calls.

Same unchanged command retried with network permission; complete private GPU qualification passed.

construction_observation: Rounding 1/6 to 0.16667 has a smaller measured complete-algorithm error than preserving more coefficient digits because its error partially offsets the omitted polynomial tail. This observation is evidence about the fixed implementation, not a separate input label.

semantic_trace_review_r1.scope: All six completed first trials. Raw traces, source and qualification evidence are unchanged. This review checks actual probe code and outputs, not verdict correctness alone.

rows.assessment: Correct reasoning without tools. The model identifies the five-decimal cubic coefficient defect and adds omitted degree-7 tail error near the first ln(2) reduction boundary. It gives an approximate legal witness near x=0.34668 and a predicted error above the mixed tolerance; independent GPU checks confirm failures there. This is a hand estimate, not executed numerical evidence or a directed FP32 error proof.

Valid actual-kernel GPU sweep of all 37,378 legal scalar encodings, including both zero encodings, against torch.expm1 in FP64. Probe t6 reports 123 violations and the same x=0.347900390625 witness as independent directed-interval qualification. One legal failing input suffices to reject the implementation.

Valid actual-kernel GPU sweeps t8/t9 enumerate 37,378 encodings and find 123 violations; t8 provides the same global worst-ratio witness as private qualification. t9 also refutes a separate large-positive-input error claim. Final Reject is supported by actual legal counterexamples.
limitations: The named k=0 region in claim c1 and t8 includes x=0.3466796875, whose actual reduction exponent is 1. The wider mask and FP16 scalar comparison do not prove the original specifically k=0 claim. The full-domain GPU failure remains valid.

Initial claims understate the permitted error near the reduction boundary and at x=10. At x=10 the tolerance is about 0.022, not 2.3e-5. Actual probes use the correct formula and rebut the latter claim.
Exhaustive scalar testing is not exhaustive testing of all tensor lengths, addresses, offsets or GPU environments.

rows.assessment: Correct final verdict based on a rough polynomial/range-reduction error estimate and source review. The reasoning contains loose or mistaken intermediate estimates of split-constant precision and hypothetical range reduction errors; it does not establish a uniform directed bound. Independent GPU qualification, not this reasoning alone, supports the Accept label.

The first probe t7 mistakenly converts integer bit patterns with to(float16), producing out-of-domain values and a validation error. The repaired t8 uses view(float16), calls the actual kernel on all 37,378 legal encodings, compares with FP64 expm1, and finds zero violations, maximum error/tolerance 0.2294604345. The repaired evidence is valid; failed t7 is retained and is not kernel-failure evidence.
limitations: The final statement that no size can fail overstates the probe. Enumerating scalar values at one tensor length does not by itself prove every length, tail, offset, input preservation or fresh allocation. These surfaces are covered separately by independent qualification and source review.

rows.assessment: Initial probe t8 incorrectly constructs negative FP16 values by negating bit-pattern integers, creates out-of-domain values, and is rejected by validation. Repaired t11 calls the actual kernel on 37,377 numerical values after torch.unique merges signed zeros, with zero violations and maximum ratio 0.2294604345. Separate t9 validly tests a contiguous offset 3 view of 1000 values and finds zero violations. The final Accept agrees with independent qualification.
limitations: 37,377 is the number of distinct numerical values after merging positive and negative zero, not all 37,378 legal encodings. The contract treats signed zeros as numerically equal, but the model did not execute both encodings in that repaired probe. Independent qualification executes both.

The field worst_abs_err=1.29146604799e-7 is absolute error at the maximum error/tolerance ratio. It is not the global maximum absolute error, which independent qualification measured as 0.00159407567844. The latter is permitted by the relative tolerance at larger outputs.
Claims of no remaining untested size, shape or storage surface overstate the evidence. Scalar enumeration and one offset example do not exhaust tensor executions.

The initial coefficient/truncation hypothesis assumes an incorrect tolerance near x=0.3466 and ignores possible cancellation between coefficient and truncation errors. Runtime evidence correctly rebuts it.

semantic_trace_review_r1.conclusion: No observed tool advantage: no-tools, Solo and Debate each classify both implementations correctly. Tools provide valid measured evidence, but the no-tool model can derive the rejecting mechanism from source and also accepts the correct control. Neither case meets the predeclared repeat criterion.
